claim: Bats host virulent zoonotic viruses without experiencing disease.
source: Bats host virulent zoonotic viruses without experiencing disease.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by citations in the introduction and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Best fit models recapitulated expected immune phenotypes for representative cell lines, supporting robust antiviral defenses in bat cells that correlated with higher estimates for within-host viral propagation rates.
source: Best fit models recapitulated expected immune phenotypes for representative cell lines, supporting robust antiviral defenses in bat cells that correlated with higher estimates for within-host viral propagation rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results presented in the manuscript, including data from Figures 1, 4, and Table 1.

claim: Heightened immune responses limit pathogen-induced cellular morbidity, which can facilitate the establishment of rapidly-propagating persistent infections within-host.
source: In general, heightened immune responses limit pathogen-induced cellular morbidity, which can facilitate the establishment of rapidly-propagating persistent infections within-host.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental results showing reduced cell mortality and elongated epidemics in bat cell cultures, as shown in Figures 1 and 5.

claim: Rapidly-transmitting viruses that have evolved with bat immune systems will likely cause enhanced virulence following emergence into secondary hosts with immune systems that diverge from those unique to bats.
source: Rapidly-transmitting viruses that have evolved with bat immune systems will likely cause enhanced virulence following emergence into secondary hosts with immune systems that diverge from those unique to bats.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the inference from the experimental and modeling results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bats are reservoir hosts for emerging viral zoonoses, including rabies and related lyssaviruses, Hendra and Nipah henipaviruses, Ebola and Marburg filoviruses, and SARS coronavirus.
source: Bats have received much attention in recent years for their role as reservoir hosts for emerging viral zoonoses, including rabies and related lyssaviruses, Hendra and Nipah henipaviruses, Ebola and Marburg filoviruses, and SARS coronavirus (Calisher et al., 2006; Wang and Anderson, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In most non-Chiropteran mammals, henipaviruses, filoviruses, and coronaviruses induce substantial morbidity and mortality, display short durations of infection, and elicit robust, long-term immunity in hosts surviving infection.
source: In most non-Chiropteran mammals, henipaviruses, filoviruses, and coronaviruses induce substantial morbidity and mortality, display short durations of infection, and elicit robust, long-term immunity in hosts surviving infection (Nicholls et al., 2003; Hooper et al., 2001; Mahanty and Bray, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Bats demonstrate no obvious disease symptoms upon infection with pathogens that are highly virulent in non-volant mammals.
source: Bats, by contrast, demonstrate no obvious disease symptoms upon infection with pathogens that are highly virulent in non-volant mammals (Schountz et al., 2017) but may, instead, support viruses as long-term persistent infections, rather than transient, immunizing pathologies (Plowright et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Bats may support viruses as long-term persistent infections, rather than transient, immunizing pathologies.
source: Bats, by contrast, demonstrate no obvious disease symptoms upon infection with pathogens that are highly virulent in non-volant mammals (Schountz et al., 2017) but may, instead, support viruses as long-term persistent infections, rather than transient, immunizing pathologies (Plowright et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Bats leverage a suite of species-specific mechanisms to limit viral load, which include host receptor sequence incompatibilities for some bat-virus combinations and constitutive expression of the antiviral cytokine, IFN-α, for others.
source: Bats leverage a suite of species-specific mechanisms to limit viral load, which include host receptor sequence incompatibilities for some bat-virus combinations (Ng et al., 2015; Takadate et al., 2020) and constitutive expression of the antiviral cytokine, IFN-α, for others (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The presence of viral RNA or DNA in the cytoplasm of mammalian cells will induce secretion of type I interferon proteins (IFN-α and IFN-β), which promote expression and translation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in neighboring cells and render them effectively antiviral.
source: Typically, the presence of viral RNA or DNA in the cytoplasm of mammalian cells will induce secretion of type I interferon proteins (IFN-α and IFN-β), which promote expression and translation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in neighboring cells and render them effectively antiviral (Stetson and Medzhitov, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature and represents established knowledge in immunology.

claim: In some bat cells, the transcriptomic blueprints for the IFN response are expressed constitutively, even in the absence of stimulation by viral RNA or DNA.
source: In some bat cells, the transcriptomic blueprints for this IFN response are expressed constitutively, even in the absence of stimulation by viral RNA or DNA (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In non-flying mammals, constitutive IFN expression would likely elicit widespread inflammation and concomitant immunopathology upon viral infection.
source: In non-flying mammals, constitutive IFN expression would likely elicit widespread inflammation and concomitant immunopathology upon viral infection, but bats support unique adaptations to combat inflammation (Zhang et al., 2013; Ahn et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2018; Pavlovich et al., 2018) that may have evolved to mitigate metabolic damage induced during flight (Kacprzyk et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established immunological knowledge.

claim: Bats support unique adaptations to combat inflammation that may have evolved to mitigate metabolic damage induced during flight.
source: In non-flying mammals, constitutive IFN expression would likely elicit widespread inflammation and concomitant immunopathology upon viral infection, but bats support unique adaptations to combat inflammation (Zhang et al., 2013; Ahn et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2018; Pavlovich et al., 2018) that may have evolved to mitigate metabolic damage induced during flight (Kacprzyk et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and involves speculation about evolutionary origins.

claim: The extent to which constitutive IFN-α expression signifies constitutive antiviral defense in the form of functional IFN-α protein remains unresolved.
source: The extent to which constitutive IFN-α expression signifies constitutive antiviral defense in the form of functional IFN-α protein remains unresolved.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: In bat cells constitutively expressing IFN-α, some protein-stimulated, downstream ISGs appear to be also constitutively expressed, but additional ISG induction is nonetheless possible following viral challenge and stimulation of IFN-β.
source: In bat cells constitutively expressing IFN-α, some protein-stimulated, downstream ISGs appear to be also constitutively expressed, but additional ISG induction is nonetheless possible following viral challenge and stimulation of IFN-β (Zhou et al., 2016; Xie et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Models of simple target cell depletion were first developed for HIV but have since been applied to other chronic infections, including hepatitis-C virus, hepatitis-B virus and cytomegalovirus.
source: Models of simple target cell depletion, in which viral load is dictated by a bottom-up resource supply of infection-susceptible host cells, were first developed for HIV (Perelson, 2002) but have since been applied to other chronic infections, including hepatitis-C virus (Neumann et al., 1998), hepatitis-B virus (Nowak et al., 1996) and cytomegalovirus (Emery et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: All three recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSV-G, rVSV-EBOV, and rVSV-MARV) infected Vero, RoNi/7.1, and PaKiT01 tissue cultures at both focal MOIs.
source: All three recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSV-G, rVSV-EBOV, and rVSV-MARV) infected Vero, RoNi/7.1, and PaKiT01 tissue cultures at both focal MOIs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Epidemics were less severe in bat cell cultures, especially when infected with the recombinant filoviruses, rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV.
source: Epidemics were less severe in bat cell cultures, especially when infected with the recombinant filoviruses, rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1 and related figures.

claim: Monolayer destruction was avoided in the case of rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells.
source: Monolayer destruction was avoided in the case of rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells: in the former, persistent viral infection was maintained throughout the 200 hr duration of each experiment, while, in the latter, infection was eliminated early in the time series, preserving a large proportion of live, uninfectious cells across the duration of the experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: For rVSV-EBOV infections on PaKiT01 cells, persistent viral infection was maintained throughout the 200 hr duration of each experiment.
source: Monolayer destruction was avoided in the case of rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells: in the former, persistent viral infection was maintained throughout the 200 hr duration of each experiment, while, in the latter, infection was eliminated early in the time series, preserving a large proportion of live, uninfectious cells across the duration of the experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: For rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells, infection was eliminated early in the time series, preserving a large proportion of live, uninfectious cells across the duration of the experiment.
source: Monolayer destruction was avoided in the case of rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells: in the former, persistent viral infection was maintained throughout the 200 hr duration of each experiment, while, in the latter, infection was eliminated early in the time series, preserving a large proportion of live, uninfectious cells across the duration of the experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The immune absent model offered the most accurate approximation of IFN-deficient Vero cell time series.
source: The absent immune model offered the most accurate approximation of IFN-deficient Vero cell time series, the induced immune model best recovered the RoNi/7.1 cell trials, and, in most cases, the constitutive immune model most closely recaptured infection dynamics across constitutively IFN-α-expressing PaKiT01 cell lines (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 4–5, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results presented in the manuscript, including data from Figure 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: The induced immune model best recovered the RoNi/7.1 cell trials.
source: The absent immune model offered the most accurate approximation of IFN-deficient Vero cell time series, the induced immune model best recovered the RoNi/7.1 cell trials, and, in most cases, the constitutive immune model most closely recaptured infection dynamics across constitutively IFN-α-expressing PaKiT01 cell lines (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 4–5, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results presented in the manuscript, including data from Figure 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: In most cases, the constitutive immune model most closely recaptured infection dynamics across constitutively IFN-α-expressing PaKiT01 cell lines.
source: The absent immune model offered the most accurate approximation of IFN-deficient Vero cell time series, the induced immune model best recovered the RoNi/7.1 cell trials, and, in most cases, the constitutive immune model most closely recaptured infection dynamics across constitutively IFN-α-expressing PaKiT01 cell lines (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 4–5, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results presented in the manuscript, including data from Figure 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: The induced immune model offered a slightly better fit than the constitutive to rVSV-MARV infections on the PaKiT01 cell line.
source: Ironically, the induced immune model offered a slightly better fit than the constitutive to rVSV-MARV infections on the PaKiT01 cell line (the one cell line-virus combination for which we know a constitutively antiviral cell-receptor incompatibility to be at play).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results presented in the manuscript.

claim: PaKiT01 cells are refractory to infection with rVSV-MARV due to incompatibilities in the NPC1 filovirus receptor.
source: Previous work in this lab has demonstrated incompatibilities in the NPC1 filovirus receptor which render PaKiT01 cells refractory to infection with rVSV-MARV (Ng and Chandrab, 2018, Unpublished results), making them structurally antiviral, over and above their constitutive expression of IFN-α.
evidence: This claim is supported by unpublished results cited in the manuscript.

claim: Pathogens can invade a host tissue culture when R0>1.
source: Pathogens can invade a host tissue culture when R0>1.
evidence: This is established knowledge in epidemiological modeling.

claim: Rapid rates of constitutive antiviral acquisition (ε) will drive R0<1: tissue cultures with highly constitutive antiviral immunity will be therefore resistant to virus invasion from the outset.
source: Rapid rates of constitutive antiviral acquisition (ε) will drive R0<1: tissue cultures with highly constitutive antiviral immunity will be therefore resistant to virus invasion from the outset.
evidence: This claim is derived from the mathematical analysis of the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: Induced immunity is stimulated following initial virus invasion, so the rate of induced antiviral acquisition (ρ) is not incorporated into the equation for R0.
source: Since, by definition, induced immunity is stimulated following initial virus invasion, the rate of induced antiviral acquisition (ρ) is not incorporated into the equation for R0; while induced immune processes can control virus after initial invasion, they cannot prevent it from occurring to begin with.
evidence: This claim is derived from the mathematical analysis of the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: At equilibrium, the theoretical, mean field model demonstrates one of three infection states: endemic equilibrium, stable limit cycles, or no infection.
source: At equilibrium, the theoretical, mean field model demonstrates one of three infection states: endemic equilibrium, stable limit cycles, or no infection (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis of the model shown in Figure 2.

claim: Endemic equilibrium is maintained when new infections are generated at the same rate at which infections are lost.
source: Theoretically, endemic equilibrium is maintained when new infections are generated at the same rate at which infections are lost, while limit cycles represent parameter space under which infectious and susceptible populations are locked in predictable oscillations.
evidence: This is established knowledge in epidemiological modeling.

claim: Limit cycles represent parameter space under which infectious and susceptible populations are locked in predictable oscillations.
source: Theoretically, endemic equilibrium is maintained when new infections are generated at the same rate at which infections are lost, while limit cycles represent parameter space under which infectious and susceptible populations are locked in predictable oscillations.
evidence: This is established knowledge in epidemiological modeling.

claim: Endemic equilibria resulting from cellular regeneration have been described in vivo for HIV and in vitro for herpesvirus plaque assays.
source: Endemic equilibria resulting from cellular regeneration (i.e. births) have been described in vivo for HIV (Coffin, 1995) and in vitro for herpesvirus plaque assays (Howat et al., 2006), but, because they so closely approach zero, true limit cycles likely only occur theoretically, instead yielding stochastic extinctions in empirical time series.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: True limit cycles likely only occur theoretically, instead yielding stochastic extinctions in empirical time series.
source: Endemic equilibria resulting from cellular regeneration (i.e. births) have been described in vivo for HIV (Coffin, 1995) and in vitro for herpesvirus plaque assays (Howat et al., 2006), but, because they so closely approach zero, true limit cycles likely only occur theoretically, instead yielding stochastic extinctions in empirical time series.
evidence: This is an inference based on the theoretical analysis and comparison with empirical observations.

claim: Regions of no infection (pathogen extinction) were bounded at lower threshold (Branch point) values for β, below which the pathogen was unable to invade.
source: Bifurcation analysis of our mean field model revealed that regions of no infection (pathogen extinction) were bounded at lower threshold (Branch point) values for β, below which the pathogen was unable to invade.
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: There is no upper threshold to invasion for β under any circumstances.
source: We found no upper threshold to invasion for β under any circumstances (i.e. β high enough to drive pathogen-induced extinction), but high β values resulted in Hopf bifurcations, which delineate regions of parameter space characterized by limit cycles.
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: High β values resulted in Hopf bifurcations, which delineate regions of parameter space characterized by limit cycles.
source: We found no upper threshold to invasion for β under any circumstances (i.e. β high enough to drive pathogen-induced extinction), but high β values resulted in Hopf bifurcations, which delineate regions of parameter space characterized by limit cycles.
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Under more robust representations of immunity, with higher values for either or both induced (ρ) and constitutive (ε) rates of antiviral acquisition, Hopf bifurcations occurred at increasingly higher values for β, meaning that persistent infections could establish at higher viral transmission rates.
source: Under more robust representations of immunity, with higher values for either or both induced (ρ) and constitutive (ε) rates of antiviral acquisition, Hopf bifurcations occurred at increasingly higher values for β, meaning that persistent infections could establish at higher viral transmission rates (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Branch point threshold for viral invasion was independent of changes to the induced immune parameter (ρ) but saturated at high values of ε that characterize highly constitutive immunity.
source: Consistent with our derivation for R0, we found that the Branch point threshold for viral invasion was independent of changes to the induced immune parameter (ρ) but saturated at high values of ε that characterize highly constitutive immunity (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Among Vero cell trials, infections with rVSV-G produced the highest β estimates, followed by infections with rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV.
source: Among Vero cell trials, infections with rVSV-G produced the highest β estimates, followed by infections with rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Figure 4.

claim: Best fit parameter estimates on Vero cell lines localized in the region of parameter space corresponding to theoretical limit cycles, consistent with observed virus-induced epidemic extinctions in stochastic tissue cultures.
source: Best fit parameter estimates on Vero cell lines localized in the region of parameter space corresponding to theoretical limit cycles, consistent with observed virus-induced epidemic extinctions in stochastic tissue cultures.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Figure 4 and the bifurcation analysis.

claim: For RoNi/7.1 cells, rVSV-G infections yielded highest β values but rVSV-MARV had higher β estimates than rVSV-EBOV.
source: As in Vero cell trials, we estimated highest β values for rVSV-G infections on RoNi/7.1 cell lines but here recovered higher β estimates for rVSV-MARV than for rVSV-EBOV.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1.

claim: More rapid rates of antiviral acquisition (either induced, ρ, constitutive, ε, or both) correlated with higher transmission rates (β).
source: In general, we observed that more rapid rates of antiviral acquisition (either induced, ρ, constitutive, ε, or both) correlated with higher transmission rates (β).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Figure 4.

claim: RoNi/7.1 parameter estimates localized in the region corresponding to endemic equilibrium for the deterministic, theoretical model.
source: RoNi/7.1 parameter estimates localized in the region corresponding to endemic equilibrium for the deterministic, theoretical model (Figure 4), yielding less acute epidemics which nonetheless went extinct in stochastic experiments.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Figure 4 and the bifurcation analysis.

claim: For all virus infections, PaKiT01 cell lines yielded β estimates a full order of magnitude higher than Vero or RoNi/7.1 cells, with each β balanced by an immune response also an order of magnitude higher than that recovered for the other cell lines.
source: For all virus infections, PaKiT01 cell lines yielded β estimates a full order of magnitude higher than Vero or RoNi/7.1 cells, with each β balanced by an immune response (either ρ, or ρ combined with ε) also an order of magnitude higher than that recovered for the other cell lines (Figure 4; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Figure 4.

claim: PaKiT01 parameter fits localized in the region corresponding to endemic equilibrium for the deterministic theoretical model.
source: As in RoNi/7.1 cells, PaKiT01 parameter fits localized in the region corresponding to endemic equilibrium for the deterministic theoretical model.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Figure 4 and the bifurcation analysis.

claim: Constitutive immune fits to rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cell lines consistently localized at or below the Branch point threshold for virus invasion (R0=1).
source: Because constitutive immune processes can actually prohibit initial pathogen invasion, constitutive immune fits to rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cell lines consistently localized at or below the Branch point threshold for virus invasion (R0=1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates and bifurcation analysis.

claim: In all model fits assuming constitutive immunity, across all cell lines, parameter estimates for ρ and ε traded off, with one parameter optimized at values approximating zero, such that the immune response was modeled as almost entirely induced or entirely constitutive.
source: In all model fits assuming constitutive immunity, across all cell lines, parameter estimates for ρ and ε traded off, with one parameter optimized at values approximating zero, such that the immune response was modeled as almost entirely induced or entirely constitutive (Table 1; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: For RoNi/7.1 cells, even when constitutive immunity was allowed, the immune response was estimated as almost entirely induced.
source: For RoNi/7.1 cells, even when constitutive immunity was allowed, the immune response was estimated as almost entirely induced, while for rVSV-G and rVSV-EBOV fits on PaKiT01 cells, the immune response optimized as almost entirely constitutive.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1.

claim: For rVSV-G and rVSV-EBOV fits on PaKiT01 cells, the immune response optimized as almost entirely constitutive.
source: For RoNi/7.1 cells, even when constitutive immunity was allowed, the immune response was estimated as almost entirely induced, while for rVSV-G and rVSV-EBOV fits on PaKiT01 cells, the immune response optimized as almost entirely constitutive.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1.

claim: PaKiT01 cell lines were by far the most antiviral of any in the study—with initial antiviral rates estimated several orders of magnitude higher than any others in the study, under either induced or constitutive assumptions.
source: Nonetheless, as hypothesized, PaKiT01 cell lines were by far the most antiviral of any in our study—with initial antiviral rates estimated several orders of magnitude higher than any others in our study, under either induced or constitutive assumptions (Table 1; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: RoNi/7.1 cells displayed the second-most-pronounced signature of immunity, followed by Vero cells, for which the initial antiviral rate was essentially zero even under forced assumptions of induced or constitutive immunity.
source: RoNi/7.1 cells displayed the second-most-pronounced signature of immunity, followed by Vero cells, for which the initial antiviral rate was essentially zero even under forced assumptions of induced or constitutive immunity (Table 1; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 4.

claim: R0 was essentially unchanged across differing immune assumptions for RoNi/7.1 and Vero cells, for which the initial antiviral rate was low.
source: We found that R0 was essentially unchanged across differing immune assumptions for RoNi/7.1 and Vero cells, for which the initial antiviral rate was low.
evidence: This claim is supported by the R0 calculations shown in Table 1.

claim: In the case of PaKiT01 cells, a high initial antiviral rate under either induced or constitutive immunity resulted in a correspondingly high estimation of β (and, consequently, R0) which still produced the same epidemic curve that resulted from the much lower estimates for β and R0 paired with absent immunity.
source: In the case of PaKiT01 cells, a high initial antiviral rate under either induced or constitutive immunity resulted in a correspondingly high estimation of β (and, consequently, R0) which still produced the same epidemic curve that resulted from the much lower estimates for β and R0 paired with absent immunity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the parameter estimates and model fits shown in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: Antiviral immune responses protect host tissues against virus-induced cell mortality and may facilitate the establishment of more rapid within-host transmission rates.
source: These findings suggest that antiviral immune responses protect host tissues against virus-induced cell mortality and may facilitate the establishment of more rapid within-host transmission rates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling and experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Total monolayer destruction occurred in all cell-virus combinations excepting rVSV-EBOV infections on RoNi/7.1 cells and rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells.
source: Total monolayer destruction occurred in all cell-virus combinations excepting rVSV-EBOV infections on RoNi/7.1 cells and rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Monolayer destruction corresponded to susceptible cell depletion and epidemic turnover where R-effective was reduced below one.
source: Monolayer destruction corresponded to susceptible cell depletion and epidemic turnover where R-effective (the product of R0 and the proportion susceptible) was reduced below one (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model results shown in Figure 5.

claim: For rVSV-EBOV infections on RoNi/7.1, induced antiviral cells safeguarded remnant live cells, which birthed new susceptible cells late in the time series.
source: For rVSV-EBOV infections on RoNi/7.1, induced antiviral cells safeguarded remnant live cells, which birthed new susceptible cells late in the time series.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model results shown in Figure 5.

claim: In rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells, antiviral protection halted the epidemic before susceptibles fully declined.
source: In rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells, this antiviral protection halted the epidemic (Figure 5; R-effective <1) before susceptibles fully declined.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model results shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the case of rVSV-EBOV on PaKiT01, the birth of new susceptibles from remnant live cells protected by antiviral status maintained late-stage transmission to facilitate long-term epidemic persistence.
source: In the case of rVSV-EBOV on PaKiT01, the birth of new susceptibles from remnant live cells protected by antiviral status maintained late-stage transmission to facilitate long-term epidemic persistence.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Models were unable to reproduce the longer-term infectious time series captured in data from rVSV-EBOV infections on PaKiT01 cell lines without incorporation of cell births.
source: Importantly, under fixed parameter values for the infection incubation rate (σ) and infection-induced mortality rate (α), models were unable to reproduce the longer-term infectious time series captured in data from rVSV-EBOV infections on PaKiT01 cell lines without incorporation of cell births, an assumption adopted in previous modeling representations of IFN-mediated viral dynamics in tissue culture (Howat et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by the modeling results and comparison with data.

claim: Cellular reproduction took place as plaque assays achieved confluency.
source: In our experiments, we observed that cellular reproduction took place as plaque assays achieved confluency.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments.

claim: Bat cell lines demonstrated a signature of enhanced interferon-mediated immune response, of either constitutive or induced form, which allowed for establishment of rapid within-host, cell-to-cell virus transmission rates (β).
source: Critically, we found that bat cell lines demonstrated a signature of enhanced interferon-mediated immune response, of either constitutive or induced form, which allowed for establishment of rapid within-host, cell-to-cell virus transmission rates (β).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results and bifurcation analysis.

claim: The antiviral state induced by the interferon pathway protects live cells from mortality in tissue culture, resulting in in vitro epidemics of extended duration that enhance the probability of establishing a long-term persistent infection.
source: Additionally, we demonstrated that the antiviral state induced by the interferon pathway protects live cells from mortality in tissue culture, resulting in in vitro epidemics of extended duration that enhance the probability of establishing a long-term persistent infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental and modeling results shown in Figures 1, 5, and Videos 1-3.

claim: Viruses evolved in bat reservoirs possessing enhanced IFN capabilities could achieve more rapid within-host transmission rates without causing pathology to their hosts.
source: Our findings suggest that viruses evolved in bat reservoirs possessing enhanced IFN capabilities could achieve more rapid within-host transmission rates without causing pathology to their hosts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Rapidly-reproducing viruses would likely generate extreme virulence upon spillover to hosts lacking similar immune capacities to bats.
source: Such rapidly-reproducing viruses would likely generate extreme virulence upon spillover to hosts lacking similar immune capacities to bats.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the inference from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Constitutive immune processes can prohibit pathogen invasion, while induced responses, by definition, can only control infections post-hoc.
source: Constitutive immune processes can thus prohibit pathogen invasion, while induced responses, by definition, can only control infections post-hoc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical analysis of the model.

claim: Assumptions of constitutive immunity will limit the cellular mortality (virulence) incurred at high transmission rates.
source: Once thresholds for pathogen invasion have been met, assumptions of constitutive immunity will limit the cellular mortality (virulence) incurred at high transmission rates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical analysis and experimental results.

claim: Interferon-stimulated antiviral cells appear to play a key role in maintaining longer term or persistent infections by safeguarding susceptible cells from rapid infection and concomitant cell death.
source: Regardless of mechanism (induced or constitutive), interferon-stimulated antiviral cells appear to play a key role in maintaining longer term or persistent infections by safeguarding susceptible cells from rapid infection and concomitant cell death.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Simple target cell models that ignore the effects of immunity best recapitulated infectious time series derived from IFN-deficient Vero cells.
source: Simple target cell models that ignore the effects of immunity best recapitulated infectious time series derived from IFN-deficient Vero cells, while models assuming induced immune processes most accurately reproduced trials derived from RoNi/7.1 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) cells, which possess a standard virus-induced IFN-response.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results.

claim: Models assuming induced immune processes most accurately reproduced trials derived from RoNi/7.1 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) cells, which possess a standard virus-induced IFN-response.
source: Simple target cell models that ignore the effects of immunity best recapitulated infectious time series derived from IFN-deficient Vero cells, while models assuming induced immune processes most accurately reproduced trials derived from RoNi/7.1 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) cells, which possess a standard virus-induced IFN-response.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results.

claim: In most cases, models assuming constitutive immune processes best recreated virus epidemics produced on PaKiT01 (Pteropus alecto) cells, which are known to constitutively express the antiviral cytokine, IFN-α.
source: In most cases, models assuming constitutive immune processes best recreated virus epidemics produced on PaKiT01 (Pteropus alecto) cells, which are known to constitutively express the antiviral cytokine, IFN-α (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting results and citation to published literature.

claim: Model support for induced immune assumptions in fits to rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells suggests that the constitutive IFN-α expression characteristic of P. alecto cells may represent more of a constitutive immune priming process than a perpetual, functional, antiviral defense.
source: Model support for induced immune assumptions in fits to rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells suggests that the constitutive IFN-α expression characteristic of P. alecto cells may represent more of a constitutive immune priming process than a perpetual, functional, antiviral defense.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model fitting results.

claim: Assumptions of simple target-cell depletion can often provide satisfactory approximations of viral dynamics, especially those reproduced in simple in vitro systems.
source: As previously demonstrated in within-host models for HIV (Coffin, 1995; Perelson et al., 1996; Nowak et al., 1995; Bonhoeffer et al., 1997; Ho et al., 1995), assumptions of simple target-cell depletion can often provide satisfactory approximations of viral dynamics, especially those reproduced in simple in vitro systems.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Model fitting emphasizes the need for incorporation of top-down effects of immune control in order to accurately reproduce infectious time series derived from bat cell tissue cultures, especially those resulting from the robustly antiviral PaKiT01 P. alecto cell line.
source: Critically, our model fitting emphasizes the need for incorporation of top-down effects of immune control in order to accurately reproduce infectious time series derived from bat cell tissue cultures, especially those resulting from the robustly antiviral PaKiT01 P. alecto cell line.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model fitting results.

claim: Enhanced IFN-mediated immune pathways in bat reservoirs may promote elevated within-host virus replication rates prior to cross-species emergence.
source: These findings indicate that enhanced IFN-mediated immune pathways in bat reservoirs may promote elevated within-host virus replication rates prior to cross-species emergence.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Bats appear to merit the title of pathogen reservoir, supporting long-term persistence of highly transmissible viral infections in isolated island populations well below expected critical community sizes.
source: Endemic maintenance of infection is a defining characteristic of a pathogen reservoir (Haydon et al., 2002), and bats appear to merit such a title, supporting long-term persistence of highly transmissible viral infections in isolated island populations well below expected critical community sizes (Peel et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Field data are difficult to reconcile without acknowledgement of a role for persistent infections.
source: Researchers debate the relative influence of population-level and within-host mechanisms which might explain these trends (Plowright et al., 2016), but increasingly, field data are difficult to reconcile without acknowledgement of a role for persistent infections (Peel et al., 2018; Brook et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Within-host persistence is supported by robust antiviral responses characteristic of bat immune processes.
source: We present general methods to study cross-scale viral dynamics, which suggest that within-host persistence is supported by robust antiviral responses characteristic of bat immune processes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental and modeling results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Viruses which evolve rapid replication rates under robust antiviral defenses may pose the greatest hazard for cross-species pathogen emergence into spillover hosts with immune systems that differ from those unique to bats.
source: Viruses which evolve rapid replication rates under these robust antiviral defenses may pose the greatest hazard for cross-species pathogen emergence into spillover hosts with immune systems that differ from those unique to bats.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the inference from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Vero cells are IFN-defective and thus limited in antiviral capacity.
source: We conducted plaque assays on six-well plate monolayers of three immortalized mammalian kidney cell lines: [1] Vero (African green monkey) cells, which are IFN-defective and thus limited in antiviral capacity (Desmyter et al., 1968);
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: RoNi/7.1 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) cells demonstrate idiosyncratic induced interferon responses upon viral challenge.
source: [2] RoNi/7.1 (Rousettus aegyptiacus) cells which demonstrate idiosyncratic induced interferon responses upon viral challenge (Kuzmin et al., 2017; Arnold et al., 2018; Biesold et al., 2011; Pavlovich et al., 2018);
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PaKiT01 (Pteropus alecto) cells constitutively express IFN-α.
source: and [3] PaKiT01 (Pteropus alecto) cells which constitutively express IFN-α (Zhou et al., 2016; Crameri et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV are recombinants for which cell entry is mediated by the glycoprotein of the bat-evolved filoviruses, Ebola (EBOV) and Marburg (MARV).
source: Two of these viruses, rVSV-EBOV and rVSV-MARV, are recombinants for which cell entry is mediated by the glycoprotein of the bat-evolved filoviruses, Ebola (EBOV) and Marburg (MARV), thus allowing us to modulate the extent of structural, as well as immunological, antiviral defense at play in each infection.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Between 18 and 39 trials were run at each cell-virus-MOI combination, excepting rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells at MOI = 0.001, for which only eight trials were run.
source: Between 18 and 39 trials were run at each cell-virus-MOI combination, excepting rVSV-MARV infections on PaKiT01 cells at MOI = 0.001, for which only eight trials were run (see Materials and methods; Figure 1—figure supplements 1–3, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Plaque assays restrict viral transmission neighbor-to-neighbor in two-dimensional cellular space.
source: Because plaque assays restrict viral transmission neighbor-to-neighbor in two-dimensional cellular space (Howat et al., 2006), we were able to track the spread of GFP-expressing virus-infected cells across tissue monolayers via inverted fluorescence microscopy.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature and represents established knowledge about plaque assays.

claim: Generalized additive models were used to infer the time course of all cell culture replicates and construct the multi-trial dataset.
source: We used generalized additive models to infer the time course of all cell culture replicates and construct the multi-trial dataset to which we eventually fit our mechanistic transmission model for each cell line-virus-specific combination (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplements 1–5).
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis methods.

claim: Vero cells possess an IFN-β deficiency.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that all cell lines used are capable of mounting a type I IFN response upon viral challenge, with the exception of Vero cells, which possess an IFN-β deficiency (Desmyter et al., 1968; Rhim et al., 1969; Emeny and Morgan, 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: RoNi/7.1 cells have been shown to mount idiosyncratic induced IFN defenses upon viral infection.
source: RoNi/7.1 cells have been shown to mount idiosyncratic induced IFN defenses upon viral infection (Pavlovich et al., 2018; Kuzmin et al., 2017; Arnold et al., 2018; Kühl et al., 2011; Biesold et al., 2011),
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Results from qPCR were consistent with the literature, indicating a less pronounced role for interferon defense against viral infection in RoNi/7.1 versus PaKiT01 cells.
source: Results were consistent with the literature, indicating a less pronounced role for interferon defense against viral infection in RoNi/7.1 versus PaKiT01 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: Replication-capable recombinant vesicular stomatitis Indiana viruses, expressing filovirus glycoproteins in place of wild type G (rVSV-G, rVSV-EBOV, and rVSV-MARV) have been previously described.
source: Replication-capable recombinant vesicular stomatitis Indiana viruses, expressing filovirus glycoproteins in place of wild type G (rVSV-G, rVSV-EBOV, and rVSV-MARV) have been previously described (Wong et al., 2010; Miller et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Immortalized kidney cell lines of Rousettus aegyptiacus (RoNi/7.1) and Pteropus alecto (PaKiT01) exhibit different innate antiviral immune phenotypes through, respectively, induced and constitutive expression of type I interferon genes.
source: Previously published work indicates that immortalized kidney cell lines of Rousettus aegyptiacus (RoNi/7.1) and Pteropus alecto (PaKiT01) exhibit different innate antiviral immune phenotypes through, respectively, induced (Biesold et al., 2011; Pavlovich et al., 2018; Kühl et al., 2011; Arnold et al., 2018) and constitutive (Zhou et al., 2016) expression of type I interferon genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The birth rate, b, and natural mortality rate, μ, balance to yield a population-level growth rate, such that it is impossible to estimate both b and μ simultaneously from total population size data alone.
source: The birth rate, b, and natural mortality rate, μ, balance to yield a population-level growth rate, such that it is impossible to estimate both b and μ simultaneously from total population size data alone.
evidence: This is established knowledge in population modeling.

claim: The natural mortality rate, μ, corresponds to a lifespan of approximately 121, 191, and 84 hours, respectively, for Vero, RoNi/7.1, and PaKiT01 cell lines.
source: This yielded a natural mortality rate, μ, corresponding to a lifespan of approximately 121, 191, and 84 hours, respectively, for Vero, RoNi/7.1, and PaKiT01 cell lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by the model fitting to control data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claim: The virus incubation rate, σ, was fixed as the inverse of the shortest observed duration of time from initial infection to the observation of the first infectious cells via fluorescent microscope for all nine cell line – virus combinations (ranging 6 to 9.5 hours).
source: We then fixed the virus incubation rate, σ, as the inverse of the shortest observed duration of time from initial infection to the observation of the first infectious cells via fluorescent microscope for all nine cell line – virus combinations (ranging 6 to 9.5 hours).
evidence: This is a description of how a model parameter was determined from experimental observations.

claim: The infection-induced mortality rate, α, was fixed at 1/6, an accepted standard for general viral kinetics.
source: We fixed α, the infection-induced mortality rate, at 1/6, an accepted standard for general viral kinetics (Howat et al., 2006),
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The rate of antiviral cell regression to susceptible status, c, was held at 0 for the timespan (<200 hours) of the experimental cell line infection trials.
source: and held c, the rate of antiviral cell regression to susceptible status, at 0 for the timespan (<200 hours) of the experimental cell line infection trials.
evidence: This is a description of a modeling assumption based on the experimental timeframe.

claim: In spatial simulations, the birth rate, b, was increased to six times the value used in the mean field model.
source: To compensate for higher thresholds to cellular persistence and virus invasion which occur under local spatial conditions (Webb et al., 2007), we increased the birth rate, b, and the cell-to-cell transmission rate, β, respectively, to six and ten times the values used in the mean field model (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a description of the spatial modeling approach, with justification from published literature.

claim: In spatial simulations, the cell-to-cell transmission rate, β, was increased to ten times the value used in the mean field model.
source: To compensate for higher thresholds to cellular persistence and virus invasion which occur under local spatial conditions (Webb et al., 2007), we increased the birth rate, b, and the cell-to-cell transmission rate, β, respectively, to six and ten times the values used in the mean field model (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a description of the spatial modeling approach, with justification from published literature.

claim: In spatial simulations, antiviral cells acted as 'refugia' which protected live cells from infection as each initial epidemic wave 'washed' across a cell monolayer.
source: In immune capable time series, spatial antiviral cells acted as 'refugia' which protected live cells from infection as each initial epidemic wave 'washed' across a cell monolayer.
evidence: This claim is supported by the spatial simulation results shown in Videos 1-3 and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Eventual birth of new susceptibles from living refugia allowed for sustained epidemic transmission in cases where some infectious cells persisted at later timepoints in simulation.
source: Eventual birth of new susceptibles from these living refugia allowed for sustained epidemic transmission in cases where some infectious cells persisted at later timepoints in simulation (Videos 1–3; Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the spatial simulation results shown in Videos 1-3 and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.
